summary: Protect paper and digital records with lifecycle controls, retention, access governance, and recovery planning. Build practical tools during training.
lede: Records resilience training helps records and information-governance professionals protect, retrieve, and recover trustworthy records across paper and digital repositories. Through practical exercises, participants classify records by business value, document retention and disposition decisions, govern access, and prioritize recovery requirements using inventories, risk registers, and continuity plans.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for preserving, governing, retrieving, or recovering organisational records. It suits beginner and intermediate practitioners who need a structured approach to records resilience across paper and electronic environments.
prerequisites: Working exposure to records management, information governance, compliance, legal administration, document control, or business continuity is recommended. You should be able to describe your organisation's main paper and electronic repositories, although you do not need prior certification or programming experience. Coding is not required. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted classification, automated retention, and immutable storage receive conceptual and operational treatment rather than technical engineering or production deployment.
